question: What are the main benefits of MCLR to customers?
options: They do not have to provide any documents
They do not need to go to the bank
They never have to repay the loan
When the Reserve Bank reduces the rates, their loans also become cheaper.
solution: MCLR has ushered in a new era of transparency in the banking system.

question: What is the impact on wealth creation when CRR increases?
solution: An increase in CRR reduces the money multiplier thereby reducing the total money supply in the economy.

question: What special power is left with the Governor of the Reserve Bank after the formation of MPC?
options: They alone can decide the repo rate
They can order the government to reduce taxes
Power to cast casting vote in case of tie
solution: The casting vote represents an important but limited power in the Governor's Committee.

question: What instruments does the Reserve Bank of India use to achieve its monetary policy objectives?
solution: Quantitative tools affect the entire economy while qualitative tools affect specific sectors.

question: What is it called if a bank is unable to pay its liabilities?
solution: Reserves (CRR, SLR) are created to protect banks from such insolvency situations.

question: What do time liabilities include in NDTL?
options: Fixed Term Deposits and Recurring Deposits
Cash kept in the bank's safe is the bank's own asset and not a liability of the depositors.
solution: Time liabilities provide banks with a stable basis for long-term investment and lending.

question: What does dovish monetary policy indicate?
options: Reduction in interest rates and focus on growth
Stopping the printing of currency completely
solution: A dovish central bank prioritizes growth over inflation control.

question: What is the effect on home loan installments if repo rate increases?
solution: Changes in repo rates have the sharpest impact on floating rate loans.

question: On what basis are MPC decisions taken?
options: Based on the majority of members
Only with the consent of the government members
solution: The reasons behind the decisions taken after the MPC meeting are made public.

question: What is the difference between repo rate and reverse repo rate called?
solution: The shorter the corridor, the more stable short-term interest rates will remain.

question: What can be the maximum range of SLR?
solution: SLR is used to maintain liquidity of banks and government borrowings.

question: What is the advantage of keeping SLR in securities instead of cash?
options: Banks do not make any profit
solution: SLR strikes a balance between the safety and profitability of banks.

question: Who is the Chairman of MPC?
solution: The Governor has an additional casting vote in the MPC which he or she uses in case of a tie.

question: What effect does monetary policy have on the growth of the economy?
options: It promotes development by reducing taxes.
Promotes investment and consumption through favorable interest rates
solution: Striking a balance between growth and inflation is the hallmark of successful monetary policy.

question: What changes does the government make in taxes when it has to control inflation?
solution: Increasing taxes is an effective fiscal way to reduce disposable income.

question: What is the quorum or minimum attendance of members for MPC meeting?
options: Just having a Governor is enough
solution: Quorum ensures that decisions taken are the result of extensive discussion.

question: What is the main difference between demand deposit and time deposit?
options: Check book is not available on time deposits.
Demand Deposit is only for the poor
Time Deposit can be withdrawn only after a certain period
Higher interest is available on demand deposits
solution: Time deposits are more secure for banks as they can invest this money for a longer period.

question: What is the main feature of Special Deposit Facility?
options: In this the interest rate is always higher than the repo rate
This is available only for foreign banks
It allows banks to deposit additional money without any collateral
solution: SDF is a more effective and flexible means of extracting liquidity from the market.

question: When is marginal standing facility useful for banks?
options: It allows banks to borrow money overnight when they are in dire straits of funds and have an emergency situation.
When they have to buy new buildings
When they have a lot of extra money they use reverse repo.
solution: The MSF rate is always higher than the repo rate so banks use it as the last option.

question: What effect does a decrease in money supply have on interest rates?
solution: The Reserve Bank attempts to control the money supply by increasing interest rates.

question: What is the impact of premature withdrawal of fixed deposits?
options: The bank makes some reduction in the rate of interest and imposes penalty
The customer has to donate all the money to the bank
The bank sends the customer to jail
solution: Fixed deposits are the most important part of time liabilities for banks.

question: What is the impact of reducing subsidies on the economy?
options: Prices of goods and services increase
There is a huge increase in production
solution: Reducing subsidies is a contractionary fiscal measure used to reduce the deficit.

question: What is 'capital' in a bank's balance sheet?
options: The positive difference between assets and liabilities
Only loan taken from Reserve Bank
All the gold held with the bank
Total number of branches of the bank
solution: Capital provides a safety net to the bank in times of losses.

question: What is the purpose of changing margin requirements for loans?
options: Limiting excessive lending to non-essential sectors
Giving equal credit to all sectors
solution: Margins for the agricultural sector are kept low so that farmers can easily get loans.

question: What does 'G-Sec' mean in monetary policy?
solution: G-Secs are considered to be the safest investments as they are backed by the government.

question: What is that part of fiscal policy that shows the difference between tax and expenditure called?
solution: Controlling fiscal deficit is an important long-term goal of fiscal policy.

question: When is the currency multiplier 'one'?
options: When CRR is zero then the multiplier will become infinite.
When the repo rate is too high
When there are no banks in the economy
solution: Lower the CRR, faster will be the pace of money creation.

question: Under what circumstances does the Reserve Bank use the special deposit facility?
options: When banks have a severe shortage of cash, then MSF or Repo is used.
When the government has to present a new budget
When the stock market is falling
solution: SDF has freed the Reserve Bank from the limits on the availability of government securities.

question: Monetary Policy Committee was established on the recommendations of which committee?
solution: Urjit Patel Committee itself had suggested inflation targeting to control inflation.

question: What is another name for contractionary monetary policy?
solution: Tight monetary policy is used when there is a lot of cash inflow into the economy.

question: What is the effect of increasing the down payment under consumer loan regulations?
solution: This tool is particularly effective at suppressing demand during periods of high inflation.

question: What will the Reserve Bank do with government securities if there is too much liquidity in the market?
options: Will sell them in the market
Will stop paying interest on securities
Will buy more securities from the market
solution: Sale of securities under OMO is a contractionary measure.

question: What is the regulation of money supply and interest rates in the economy called?
solution: The main goal of monetary policy is to control inflation and promote sustainable growth.

question: What is the ultimate impact of monetary policy?
options: Only those who invest in the stock market
It affects everyone's budget through interest rates and inflation on the purchasing power and cost of living of the common man.
Only on the employees of the Reserve Bank
solution: Correct implementation of monetary policy is the key to an inclusive and stable growth.

question: What effect does increasing bank rates have on the economy?
options: Borrowing becomes expensive and the money supply decreases
There is a sudden boom in investment
solution: An increase in the bank rate is a signal of a contractionary monetary policy.

question: What is the rate corridor of reverse repo?
options: Range between MSF and Reverse Repo
Difference between repo and base rate
Difference between bank rate and MSF
solution: This corridor helps in reducing the volatility of interest rates in the financial market.

question: What is the cash reserve ratio calculated on?
options: On Net Demand and Time Liability
solution: As the cash reserve ratio increases, the lending ability of banks decreases.

question: Why is MSF rate called 'penal rate'?
options: Because it is higher than the normal repo rate and is given at the fault or deficiency of the bank, it encourages banks to manage liquidity carefully.
Because this is the incarceration rate
Because no one wants to take loan on it
solution: The MSF rate is linked to the bank rate and remains at the top of the policy corridor.

question: What is 'transmission' of monetary policy?
options: Conversion of foreign currency into rupees is called exchange rate management.
The process of changes in policy rates reaching market interest rates
Sending notes from one bank to another
solution: The main objective of introducing MCLR was to improve monetary policy transmission.

question: What does 'marginal cost of funds' indicate for banks?
options: The cost that a bank incurs in raising an additional one rupee of deposits
The average interest paid on old deposits is based on the cost of new deposits.
solution: Marginal cost based rates allow borrowers to quickly benefit from declines in market rates.

question: In what form are banks required to maintain reserves under Statutory Liquidity Ratio?
options: Only in the form of government bonds
In the form of cash only
Only in the form of foreign currency
Cash in the form of gold and approved securities is kept with the bank to ensure liquidity.
solution: Banks keep the statutory liquidity ratio with themselves and can earn interest on it.

question: What is involved in the technique of Naitik Sujan or Moral Suasana?
options: Advising banks and persuading them to follow monetary policy
solution: The Reserve Bank often gives moral incentives to banks to pass on the benefits of interest rate cuts to customers.

question: What is liquidity?
options: Availability of cash in the economy
Solid bricks laid with the bank
solution: The main function of the Reserve Bank is to manage liquidity in the market in such a way that there is neither shortage nor excess of money.

question: What is the 'automatic stabilizer' of fiscal policy?
options: A system like income tax which automatically increases tax collection as income increases
The computer that creates the budget
solution: Automatic stabilizers help reduce the impact of economic fluctuations.

question: What does money multiplier mean?
options: Returns of investment in stock market
The total amount of debt taken by the government
The maximum extent to which the money supply can increase due to bank deposits
solution: There is an inverse relationship between the money multiplier and the reserve ratio.

question: What is one of the four main components of MCLR calculation?
options: Only the international price of gold
solution: Marginal cost of funds makes MCLR sensitive to changes in the repo rate.

question: When was MCLR introduced by the Reserve Bank?
solution: MCLR is calculated on the basis of marginal cost of funds which is different from the old base rate.

question: What are liabilities of a bank?
options: Total profit earned by the bank
The amount of depositors' deposits with the bank
solution: The deposit amount is like a loan for the bank on which it has to pay interest to the customers.

question: What does the Reserve Bank regulate under consumer credit regulation?
options: Number of installments and amount of down payment
Quality of goods purchased by consumers
solution: By increasing the amount of down payment, people make less purchases which helps in reducing inflation.

question: What is the minimum interest rate called below which banks cannot give loans to anyone?
solution: The base rate system has now been replaced by MCLR to increase transparency.

question: Where do banks keep the statutory liquidity ratio?
options: The International Monetary Fund is a global institution that does not hold the reserves of domestic banks.
The bank has to keep it with itself at the headquarters of the Reserve Bank.
solution: Through SLR the government forces banks to invest in its securities.

question: What could be an example of credit rationing?
options: Giving the same interest rate to all sectors
Fixing a limit on the total credit given by a bank to a specific industry
Giving loans only to government officials
Not asking for any documents for loan
solution: The Reserve Bank also achieves the objectives of credit rationing through priority sector lending.

question: What does it mean for the Reserve Bank to have a neutral 'view' or 'stance'?
options: He will help only government banks
He will neither increase nor decrease interest rates
He will stop making monetary policy
He will focus only on Forex
solution: The neutral stance indicates that the Reserve Bank is free to move in any direction in the future.

question: How should the sum of liabilities and assets always be in the bank balance sheet?
options: There should be no relation between the two
The sum of both should be equal
Assets should always be twice the liabilities
solution: Bank capital is actually the difference between assets and liabilities which maintains balance.

question: Who makes public the decision of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting?
options: The Governor of the Reserve Bank
solution: Along with policy announcements, future economic projections are also shared.

question: What is the bank rate currently mainly used for?
options: To provide car loans to customers
To pay salaries to the government
solution: The bank rate has now become more of a penal rate rather than a straight lending rate.

question: What is the main difference between monetary policy and fiscal policy?
options: Monetary policy focuses on the money supply and fiscal on the government budget
Fiscal policy is only for a day
Monetary policy is run by the government and fiscal policy is run by the Reserve Bank
Monetary policy is applicable only in village and fiscal in cities
solution: For economic stability, coordination between these two policies is extremely important.

question: What does 'Adjustment' mean in the Liquidity Adjustment Facility?
options: Correcting the market's short-term cash shortage or excess
solution: LAF helps banks meet their daily cash management challenges.

question: What is the main objective of maintaining cash reserve ratio and statutory liquidity ratio?
options: Limiting the lending capacity of the bank
Reducing the fiscal deficit of the government
Ensuring the financial security and liquidity of the bank
solution: These reserve requirements are essential to maintain public confidence in the banking system.

question: Why is the Reserve Bank called the 'lender of last resort'?
options: Because he prints the note last
Because he gives loans only to those banks which are about to close
Because when banks do not get loans from anywhere else, they go to the Reserve Bank
Because it gives loans directly to the customers
solution: The role of lender of last resort maintains stability and confidence in the banking system.

question: How many total members are there in the Monetary Policy Committee?
solution: Among the six members of the committee, the Governor of the Reserve Bank is its ex-officio chairman.

question: How are 'dissatisfaction' of members recorded in the MPC report?
options: By forcing him to resign from the committee
By making public their personal opinions and reasons for disagreement
solution: The MPC's minute book contains details of each member's voting and their arguments.

question: By what other name are 'quantitative' tools of monetary policy also called?
solution: CRR and Repo rate are the most effective examples of quantitative tools.

question: What are the main instruments of fiscal policy?
options: Only printing of notes is the job of the Reserve Bank.
solution: Fiscal policy is presented in Parliament every year through the Budget.

question: What is the frequency of meetings of the Monetary Policy Committee?
options: It is administratively difficult to hold meetings every month
solution: The Monetary Policy Committee is legally obliged to meet at least four times a year.

question: What is the main difference between quantitative and qualitative instruments in monetary policy instruments?
options: Quantitative tools are run by the government
Quantitative tools only affect the rich
Qualitative instruments have no effect on the money supply
solution: Quantitative instruments are called general controls and qualitative ones are called selective controls.

question: What does the Reserve Bank do in the process of sterilization?
options: Withdraws all old notes from the market
The excess liquidity generated by the inflow of foreign currency is absorbed through OMOs
solution: Sterilization is an important way to protect the economy from external financial shocks.

question: Who manages fiscal policy?
solution: The main objective of fiscal policy is to ensure economic stability and social justice.

question: What could be a 'conflict of interest' for members of the Monetary Policy Committee?
options: It is necessary for experts to be educated.
They should not be financially connected to any banking institution so that their decisions are impartial, working in any bank or getting benefits from it.
It is an essential qualification for them to be citizens of India.
solution: Members are required to declare their assets to prevent conflict of interest.

question: Who selects the three government members of the MPC?
options: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
The Governor of the Reserve Bank is directly selected by the government.
A search committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary
solution: Government members have a tenure of four years and are not eligible for reappointment.

question: What is 'reset' of interest rates under the MCLR system?
options: Changing the interest rate of the loan according to the current market rate after a certain period of time
Waiver of loan completely would be a loss for the bank.
Changing rates only for new customers
Changing the interest rate every day
solution: The reset period ensures borrowers benefit from changes in monetary policy.

question: What does 'revenue deficit' of fiscal policy indicate?
options: Total infrastructure created by the government
The excess of the government's regular expenses over its regular income shows that the government is borrowing even for its daily operations.
solution: Reducing revenue deficit is extremely important for the financial health of the government.

question: What is that part of fiscal policy that taxes more from the rich and less from the poor called?
solution: India's income tax system is an example of a progressive tax system.

question: Why is the bank rate considered a 'penalty rate'?
options: Because no one takes loan on it
Because the Reserve Bank uses it to impose penalties on banks that do not follow the rules
solution: If a bank keeps CRR less then it is penalized based on bank rate.

question: How has the formation of MPC improved the accountability of the Reserve Bank?
options: Because no interest is charged anymore
Because now the government makes all the policy
Now the Governor does not have to do any work
Because each member has to give written reasons for his/her decision
solution: Increasing accountability increases market confidence and stability in the central bank.

question: Which is an example of 'transfer payment' under fiscal policy?
solution: Transfer payments ensure redistribution in the economy.

question: What effect does fiscal policy have on the supply side of the economy?
options: It is just the act of printing notes
It stops importing goods from abroad
Increases production capacity through tax incentives and public investment
solution: Supply side reforms help reduce inflation in the long run.

question: Why did the Urjit Patel Committee suggest the formation of MPC?
options: To give complete control over the banks to the government
To limit the decision making power to the Governor only
solution: With the formation of the MPC, India has adopted a flexible inflation targeting framework.

question: What is the 'time lag' of monetary policy and fiscal policy?
options: Monetary policy decisions can be taken quickly but take time to take effect
Monetary policy is effective only in winter
Fiscal policy only works at night
solution: Monetary policy is flexible and can be changed every two months.

question: What is 'inflation targeting' of monetary policy?
options: Raising taxes in line with inflation
Maintaining inflation within a certain limit such as four percent
solution: India has set a legal target of keeping inflation between two to six percent.

question: What is the period of 'notice money' in call money market?
solution: Notice money gives banks flexibility in managing their short-term liquidity requirements.

question: What is the minimum loan amount to avail the MSF window?
options: One crore rupees and its multiples
solution: MSF is used by banks only when liquidity in the inter-bank market dries up.

question: What is an example of 'direct tax' fiscal policy?
solution: Direct taxes are progressive, meaning those with higher incomes are taxed more.

question: What qualification is mandatory for MPC members?
options: They should be well versed in law
They should be citizens of India
They should be active in politics.
solution: Members are selected on the basis of their expertise and understanding of monetary policy.

question: What do the securities approved under SLR include?
options: Bonds of central and state governments
solution: SLR ensures that a portion of banks remains available to meet government borrowing needs.

question: When is 'Wind Profit Tax' imposed as part of fiscal policy?
options: When a company is making losses
When the government has to campaign, it is only to correct economic anomalies.
When an industry has suddenly made huge profits due to external circumstances
When the public doesn't have any money
solution: Windfall profits tax is a way of raising additional revenue for social welfare.

question: Which two instruments are covered under liquidity adjustment facility?
solution: Through LAF, the Reserve Bank balances the shortage or excess of cash in the banking system.

question: What is the interest that the Reserve Bank gives to banks through 'Reverse Repo' called?
solution: The reverse repo rate sets the lower limit on interest rates in the market.

question: Repurchase obligation is part of which monetary instrument?
solution: The word 'Repo' is actually an abbreviation of 'Repurchase Agreement'.

question: The main objective of monetary policy What does 'price stability' mean?
options: Just keeping stock market prices stable
Not changing the prices of goods at all
Keeping inflation within a target range
Keeping tax rates stable can be an objective of fiscal policy.
solution: Price stability protects the purchasing power of consumers and helps in economic planning.

question: When is NDTL usually calculated?
solution: Calculation on a fortnightly basis gives banks time to balance their reserves.

question: What could be the objective of reducing the minimum support price?
options: Controlling the rise in food prices
solution: MSP is a guaranteed price given by the government to farmers for their crops.

question: What is the penalty imposed on a bank if it fails to maintain the required CRR and SLR?
options: Penalty three percent above the bank rate for each day of default
solution: This punitive interest rate forces banks to manage their reserves carefully.

question: What else are the operating procedures of an open market called?
solution: Under OMO, the Reserve Bank buys and sells government securities.

question: Which securities are used for 'sterilization' by the Reserve Bank?
options: Government securities under the Market Stabilization Scheme
solution: Sterilization is a means of controlling the sudden influx of foreign currency into the market.

question: What will be the impact on banks if CRR is abolished?
options: Their lending capacity will increase greatly
They will only buy government bonds
They will stop taking deposits from customers
solution: Expiry of CRR could create excessive liquidity and instability in the banking system.

question: What is the role of fixed deposits in NDTL?
options: It is a stable and long term source of funds for the bank
This is the immediate cash asset of the bank
Banks do not give any interest on this.
Customers can withdraw it from the ATM at any time without going to the bank.
solution: Fixed deposits help banks manage credit risk.

question: What is 'Public Debt' under fiscal policy?
options: All the money deposited with the bank
Money that the public has borrowed from banks
Only money that government distributes for free
The money that the government has borrowed from the market or abroad to meet its expenses. It is the responsibility of the government to repay it.
solution: Management of public debt is important for the sustainability of government finances.

question: Where do banks keep cash reserve ratio money?
options: It is not kept with the bank but with the Reserve Bank, in the bank's own secure locker.
solution: CRR is the most direct way of controlling the flow of cash in the banking system.

question: What are demand liabilities in Net Demand and Time Liabilities?
options: The loan that the bank has asked for
Deposits in savings and current accounts
solution: Demand liabilities are more risky for banks because their flow is uncertain.

question: What are qualitative monetary policy instruments called?
solution: Qualitative tools focus on the direction and quality of credit rather than its quantity.

question: When are taxes reduced as part of fiscal policy?
options: When inflation is very high, taxes are increased.
When the economy is going through a recession or depression, reducing taxes leaves people with more money to spend.
When the government has to repay huge debt, then the government raises revenue by increasing taxes.
solution: Tax cuts act like a 'fiscal stimulus' to accelerate growth.

question: For whom is determination of net demand and time liability important?
options: For determining the salaries of the bank's employees
solution: NDTL reflects the total deposits available with the bank at any point of time.

question: What do time liabilities represent?
options: Cash reserves held with the bank
Daily borrowings taken by the bank
Those deposits which can be withdrawn at any time are called demand liabilities.
Deposits payable after a certain period
solution: Banks generally offer higher interest on time liabilities than demand deposits.

question: What are both 'savings account' and 'current account' with the bank called?
solution: Savings accounts earn a little interest while current accounts generally earn no interest.

question: What will be the result if the Reserve Bank reduces the repo rate?
options: People will deposit more money in banks
Foreign investment will be completely stopped
Borrowing cost of banks will reduce
solution: Repo rate cut is considered an important step to accelerate economic growth.

question: What does credit rationing mean?
options: Giving loans to all without any limit
Setting loan ceilings for different sectors ensures that loan distribution is balanced and does not lead to excessive risk in any one sector.
Not charging any interest on loan
solution: Credit rationing is used when there is high demand for credit in the market and limited supply.

question: What type of relationship is there between the cash reserve ratio and the money multiplier?
options: There is a relationship only at the time of profit
solution: If CRR is increased to 100% then the money multiplier will become one and banks will not be able to give any loans.

question: What is the main difference between bank rate and repo rate?
options: Collateral is not required in bank rate
Bank rate is for short term
No interest has to be paid in repo rate
Bank rate is only for private banks
solution: The bank rate is nowadays mainly used as a basis for penalty provisions.

question: Which institutions are not required to maintain CRR and SLR?
options: NBFCs and NBFCs are not banks and only accept deposits or make specific loans.
solution: Non-banking financial companies are not part of the entire money creation process like banks.

question: What is the relationship between monetary policy and exchange rates?
options: Low interest rates always make the dollar cheaper
Higher interest rates usually strengthen the value of a currency as foreign investors demand that country's currency for greater profits.
Only gold prices decide the exchange rate
solution: The Reserve Bank tries to ensure the stability of the rupee through its monetary policy.

question: What is the bank rate?
options: On which the government borrows from the banks
On which the Reserve Bank gives long term loans to commercial banks
The rate at which banks give loans to each other is called call money rate.
The rate at which banks give loans to customers is called base rate or MCLR.
solution: The bank rate is nowadays mainly used to calculate penalty rates.

question: What is the correct combination of actions of the Reserve Bank during inflation?
options: Reduction in repo rate and CRR
Increase in Repo Rate and CRR
solution: The policy adopted during inflation is called contractionary or tight monetary policy.

question: Who do quantitative monetary policy tools affect?
options: Only to the portfolio of foreign investors
The total money supply and credit in the economy
solution: Quantitative instruments are also called general instruments because their effect is universal.

question: Who does the Reserve Bank attack through consumer credit regulation?
options: On demand-driven inflation, demand for goods is reduced by making installments expensive.
Only those who do not have a bank account
solution: This tool helps in controlling excessive consumption of luxury goods.

question: What is the main purpose of reverse repo?
options: Providing money to the government for free
Encouraging banks to give more loans
Soaking up excess liquidity from the market
solution: When the reverse repo rate increases, banks consider it safer to keep money with the Reserve Bank instead of giving loans in the market.

question: What is the definition of repo rate?
options: The rate at which commercial banks borrow from the Reserve Bank by placing government securities as collateral
The rate at which the Reserve Bank borrows from foreign banks
The rate at which banks accept deposits from customers
The rate at which banks pledge their gold with the Reserve Bank
solution: Repo rate is the most important policy rate instrument of monetary policy.

question: What is not included in 'revenue expenditure' under fiscal policy?
options: Construction of new roads and bridges
solution: Revenue expenditure does not create any new wealth.

question: Which is an example of an asset for a bank?
options: Loans and advances given by the bank
solution: When a bank gives a loan to an individual he becomes a financial asset for the bank.

question: How do MCLR rates differ from fixed loan rates?
options: MCLR rates are floating and affected by policy changes
MCLR is only for the poor
solution: Most modern home loans are linked to MCLR or external benchmark.

question: When is the 'cheap money policy' stance of monetary policy adopted?
options: When foreign debt has to be repaid
When needed to spur economic growth
Only on the first day of the New Year
When inflation is at its peak then expensive currency policy is adopted.
solution: Cheap currency policy is also called 'cheap money policy'.

question: What is the valuable thing given as guarantee for a loan called?
solution: Government securities are the most common collateral used in the repo market.

question: What is an example of 'capital expenditure' under fiscal policy?
options: Expenditure only on tea and breakfast
Payment of interest on loans taken is a mandatory revenue obligation.
solution: Capital expenditure lays the foundation for economic growth and gives returns in the long run.

question: What policy does the Reserve Bank adopt during deflation or recession?
solution: The objective of expansionary policy is to revive demand in the economy.

question: Why was MCLR introduced by reforming the base rate system?
options: Because banks were not passing on the benefit of repo rate cut to customers
Its objective was to increase the efficiency of the banking system by reducing the power of the Governor of the Reserve Bank.
solution: MCLR ensured that banks reviewed their interest rates on a monthly basis.

question: What is the tenure of non-official members of MPC?
solution: Fixed tenure allows members to take independent decisions.

question: What securities can banks access under MSF?
options: of government securities within their SLR limit
Only those who are outside the SLR quota
solution: MSF allows banks to borrow only up to a certain percentage of their NDTL.

question: What is the advantage of not requiring securities in special deposit facility?
options: Banks do not get any interest
The Reserve Bank does not have to worry about pledging its securities
The Reserve Bank has to do less work
It only works in exchange for gold
solution: SDF has removed the security related limitations of reverse repo.

question: How much interest do banks earn on money held as cash reserve ratio?
solution: Cash reserve ratio acts as an unproductive asset for banks as there is no profit on it.

question: What is the fastest way to absorb 'liquidity' under monetary policy?
solution: Increase in reverse repo rate leads to immediate shortage of money in the market.

question: When are qualitative tools used?
options: Quantitative tools are used when the entire economy is in recession.
When foreign exchange reserves become zero
When to prevent speculation or excessive credit flow in a particular sector
When the government has to win elections
solution: Qualitative tools balance the distribution of credit among different parts of the economy.

question: Which accounts are included under demand deposit?
solution: Demand deposits are used by people for their daily needs and immediate transactions.

question: For whom is MSF window available only?
options: Only for those who are very rich
solution: The MSF provides a safety valve for banks to deal with liquidity shocks.

question: What effect does increase in government expenditure have on the economy?
options: Tax rates immediately go to zero
solution: Increasing public expenditure is a major fiscal tool to accelerate economic growth.

question: What steps does the government take under expansionary fiscal policy?
options: Reduction in taxes and increase in public expenditure
Increase in taxes and decrease in spending
solution: In times of recession, governments often resort to expansionary fiscal policy to increase demand.

question: Which formula is correct for calculating money multiplier?
options: Repo Rate times C R R
solution: If CRR is four percent then the currency multiplier will be twenty-five.

question: By what other name is the policy adopted to control inflation known?
solution: Hawkish is the term used when the central bank's main focus is only on suppressing inflation.

question: What is the main goal of selective credit control?
options: Giving free loans only to the poor
To reduce the credit demand of the entire economy
It is against policy to close all private banks.
Discouraging credit flow to specific sectors such as speculative businesses
solution: Selective controls ensure that credit is used only for productive purposes.

question: What is it called when the Reserve Bank directly buys government securities?
solution: Purchasing of securities increases the flow of cash into the market.

question: What is the similarity between repo rate and bank rate?
options: Both are for overnight lending only
Both rates are set by the Reserve Bank
No interest is charged on both
solution: Both of these rates act as standards for liquidity and interest rates in the banking system.

question: What is the maximum period of borrowing in the call money market?
solution: The call money market is the main venue for balancing the daily liquidity position of banks.

question: What is the main objective of contractionary fiscal policy?
options: Reducing inflation and controlling budget deficit
solution: When the economy overheats, the government adopts contractionary policies.

question: What does 'market' mean in 'open market operations'?
options: The secondary market where government securities are traded
Stock market where Reliance shares are sold
solution: Through OMO the Reserve Bank directly influences the quantity of money in the market.

question: What is 'deficit financing' in fiscal policy?
options: Borrowing by the government to meet its expenses
Keeping the budget always in profit
solution: Balanced deficit is good for growth but excessive deficit can destabilize the economy.

question: What will banks have to do if NDTL increases?
options: They will have to waive off all the old loans
They will have to maintain proportionately higher CRR and SLR since the reserves are as a percentage of NDTL.
They have to open new branches
They have to reduce their profit
solution: The increase in NDTL is indicative of increasing confidence and deposits in the banking system.

question: What could be the negative impact of 'credit rationing' under qualitative instruments?
options: A lot of cash will be deposited with the banks
There may be a shortage of credit in some important sectors
solution: Credit rationing should be used very carefully so that economic growth is not hindered.

question: Which qualitative tool will the Reserve Bank adopt if a bank is lending to very high risk sectors?
options: Will close all the ATMs of the bank
Will increase margin requirements and exert moral pressure
solution: Selective credit controls induce banks to make safe loans.

question: What is the direct impact of increase in cash reserve ratio?
options: On the ability of banks to give loans
Only on the number of foreign tourists
solution: CRR is a powerful and immediate impact instrument of monetary policy.
